stories.headline: Kartarpur Corridor will be reopened as soon as national security concerns are resolved, says Amit Shah
stories.title: Kartarpur Corridor will be reopened as soon as national security concerns are resolved, says Amit Shah
stories.summary: “It was solely due to the carelessness of the Congress that such a sacred, major site is not a part of India today,” Amit Shah said
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in title weight 70
article_sentences: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), addressing a press meet in Punjab, said that the Kartarpur Corridor will be opened as soon as national security concerns are resolved.

Speaking at the joint press conference between the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) at the BJP headquarters at Delhi, Mr. Shah said if the BJP had been in power during the time of independence, Kartarpur Corridor would have been a part of India.
“It was solely due to the carelessness of the Congress that such a sacred, major site is not a part of India today,” he added.
The Kartarpur Corridor was built by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP initiated pilgrimage there, Mr. Shah said.
“However, after Operation Sindoor, when national security was concerned, the Corridor was closed on a temporary basis.
As soon as this issue is completely resolved, we will immediately reopen Kartarpur Sahib with full honour,” Mr. Shah said.
“One should not do politics on matters of national security,” he added.
Kartarpur Corridor is a religious, visa-free Corridor, connecting Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan with Gurdwara Dera Baba Nanak in Gurdaspur District, Punjab, India.
In November 2019, PM Modi flagged off the first batch of Indian pilgrims along the Corridor.
Since Operation Sindoor in May 2025, the Kartarpur Corridor has been closed for pilgrims.
“Considering the prevailing security scenario with Pakistan, it would not be possible to send Sikh pilgrims to Pakistan,” the Ministry of Home Affairs announced in September 2025.
Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), sent a letter to PM Modi urging him to reopen the Corridor.

stories.headline: India counters China in Nepal amid flood crisis
stories.title: India counters China in Nepal amid flood crisis
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Relations had frayed over the past decade amid border disputes and resentment over a 2015 blockade that many Nepalis blamed on New Delhi and which crippled fuel and other supplies.
India has denied it was responsible.

Over the same period, China expanded its footprint, with trade surging as electronics and electric vehicles flooded Nepali markets and Beijing extended its influence through infrastructure, health and education.
Land-locked Nepal is nestled in the Himalayas between China and India and the two Asian giants have vied for influence in the impoverished nation for decades.

China's economic rise has given Kathmandu greater room to manoeuvre between its neighbours, challenging India's longstanding assumption that geography, economic integration and cultural ties between the two Hindu-majority countries would preserve its primacy.
The floods have given Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi an opening to claw back some lost ground in the battle for influence.
India was the first foreign government to respond to one of Nepal's worst recorded disasters in August, sending relief supplies and helping restore communications.
On Monday, New Delhi followed with a $1.62 billion package of grants and credit for reconstruction, infrastructure and energy.
India extended the package when 36-year-old Shah came to New Delhi, his first bilateral visit since taking power in March.
Nepal needs about $5 billion to rebuild damaged infrastructure, nearly a tenth of its economy.
India's package is the largest financial assistance Nepal has ever received, Minister for Foreign Affairs Shisir Khanal said in a statement.
Indian aid disbursement to Nepal was over fourfold higher than that of China in the 2024-25 fiscal year that ended in mid-July, according to Nepali government data.

stories.headline: Jack Snipe, Water Rail and Vagrants: A dry Kutch forces rare birds to flood Mumbai
stories.title: Jack Snipe, Water Rail and Vagrants: A dry Kutch forces rare birds to flood Mumbai
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Migration season has descended upon the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, as flocks of birds swarm over wetlands, saltpans and marshes on the way to their winter destinations.
But amid the usual suspects, some have caused the hearts of birders to go aflutter.
Word around town — and in WhatsApp groups — is that the passage migrants which typically make their fueling stops up in the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat are coming more southward.
The MMR is the lucky winner.
The Jack Snipe, a small speckled and stripy bird with a pointy thin bill, shy and great at camouflage, is one of the celebrities.
“Gentleman Jack,” “Jackie Dada,” the bird has been spotted at the Gogte Saltpans in Vasai and TS Chanakya in Navi Mumbai since the beginning of November.

“If there is any disturbance, the Jack Snipes take cover in the reeds,” said Raju Kasambe, ornithologist, Maharashtra state coordinator of the Asian Waterbird Census and founder of Mumbai Bird Katta, who spotted them in mid-November and was at TS Chanakya on Sunday to catch another sight, among many birders standing guard.
“Usually, the birds make a stopover for a few days up to a fortnight in the northern drier parts of Gujarat, and then go on to their destinations in Africa.
But a possible reason why they’re flocking towards the MMR is that there has been very scanty rainfall this year in Kutch,” said Kasambe.
Then there is the Red-backed Shrike and the Red-tailed Shrike.
“These are typically dry desert and thorny forest birds, which is not a habitat present much around the MMR.
But the lack of availability of food has likely driven them here,” he said.

stories.headline: Ousted leader Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on Dec 16, spokesperson says
stories.title: Ousted leader Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on Dec 16, spokesperson says
stories.summary: Dhaka, Nov 24: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, the day the country celebrates as Victory Day when it won independence after a war with Pakistan. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule. She was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity involving the uprising in which hundreds of protesters were killed. Hasina rejected the verdict and has said she is ready fight the case once she is back. In the statement Tuesday announcing the planned date of her return, she urged current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline. “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali said in the statement. “It is deeply symbolic that she has chosen 16 December, our Victory Day, for her planned return to Bangladesh. We firmly believe that she will celebrate this historic day among her people, honouring the great victory achieved under the leadership of her father, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman," Abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Hasina, told The Associated Press. “We are equally confident that, she will definitely return and under her leadership post return, Bangladesh will once again advance towards peace, stability and prosperity,” Arin said. Earlier this month, in an interview with The Associated Press, Hasina said she would return to the country in December at any cost, and even death could not prevent her from returning home.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Stays Kerala High Court Judgment Allowing Restructuring Of Police Associations And Abolition Of KPOA
stories.title: Supreme Court Stays Kerala High Court Judgment Allowing Restructuring Of Police Associations And Abolition Of KPOA
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has stayed a Kerala High Court judgment which had upheld the State government's decision to restructure recognised police associations in Kerala by abolishing the Kerala.
Police Officers' Association (KPOA) and redistributing its members between two other associations.

A bench of Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva put on hold the Division Bench ruling of November 12, 2026, which had set aside a Single Judge decision quashing the government's restructuring order dated July 27, 2026.
The dispute concerns a government order reorganising the three recognised police associations in the State – the Kerala.
Police Association (KPA), the Kerala.
Police Officers' Association (KPOA) and the Kerala.
Police Senior Officers' Association (KPSOA).
Under the restructuring, the State had decided to abolish the KPOA and redistribute its members between the KPA and KPSOA.
The arrangement envisaged bringing Civil.
Police Officers, Senior Civil Police.

Officers, Grade Assistant Sub Inspectors, Assistant Sub Inspectors and Grade Sub Inspectors under the KPA, while directly recruited Sub Inspectors and officers in the regular promotional hierarchy, including Inspectors, Deputy Superintendents of Police and Superintendents of Police (Non-IPS), would be grouped under the KPSOA.

The associations challenged the government order before the Kerala High Court, arguing that the existing associations functioned under government-approved bylaws and their organisational structure could not be altered contrary to those rules.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice On PIL Against MPs/MLAs Resigning To Evade Anti-Defection Law
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On PIL Against MPs/MLAs Resigning To Evade Anti-Defection Law
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23) issued notice on a PIL seeking safeguards against Members of Parliament and State Legislatures using strategically timed resignations to avoid disqualification proceedings under the 10th Schedule of the Constitution (the anti-defection law).
A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana sought responses of the Union Government, the Election Commission of India, the Law Commission of India.
Senior Advocate A. Sirajudeen appeared for the petitioner (A Sethu).

The case has been tagged with another plea raising the issue of election expenditure recovery from a candidate who resigns after getting elected from one political party in order to recontest from another party (Ref: K Suthan.
Union of India).

The PIL raises concerns that legislators facing/anticipating disqualification proceedings frequently tender their resignations before the Speaker or Chairman of the House can adjudicate the allegations of defection on merits.

It contends that such resignations, alongwith prolonged delays in disposal of disqualification petitions, enable legislators to evade the consequences contemplated under the 10th Schedule and facilitate political realignments that may alter the fate of elected governments.
Referring to Shrimanth Balasaheb Patil.

Hon'ble Speaker, Karnataka Legislative Assembly, the petitioner argues that resignation and disqualification operate in distinct constitutional fields and that resignation after a disqualifying act does not extinguish proceedings relating to alleged defection.

"A resignation process that can be used to postpone, and then to avoid, the consequences of defection, coupled with the absence of any enforced time-limit for deciding disqualification petitions, impairs the integrity of the electoral mandate”, the plea states.

It is further the petitioner's contention that by the time disqualification proceedings are eventually decided, the term of the House may have expired, a by-election may have taken place, or the Government may have fallen or survived, thereby rendering the adjudication ineffective.
The petitioner relies upon the Supreme Court's decisions in Kihoto Hollohan.

stories.headline: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on deepathoon at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement
stories.title: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on deepathoon at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement
stories.summary: A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) allowed the lighting of the lamp, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, on the deepathoonat the Thirupparankundram Hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district on Karthigai Deepam day (November 24).

A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice.
The court issued notice on the appeals filed by the State.
The interim order dealt with pleas by the State to stay the January 6 judgment and looked into the question whether the lamp could be lit on the deepathoon on the coming Karthigai Deepam day.
“What weighs with us at this stage is the peculiar nature of the occasion and the proximity of the festival, which is scheduled to take place on November 24.
The opportunity to perform the ceremony on that particular day, if denied, cannot be restored by any subsequent adjudication.
Equally, we are conscious that the performance of the ceremony, once permitted, cannot be undone,” said the order.

The Bench, comprising Justice P.B. Varale, said there was a need to balance the immediacy of the festival with the need to ensure that the interim order would not prejudice the appeal of the State or become fodder for claims of a vested right.
“We are of the view that a limited, one-time arrangement, subject to stringent safeguards, would appropriately balance the interests involved pending further consideration,” the court observed.
Imposing a series of restrictions and safeguards, the court directed that the Subramaniya Swamy Temple Devasthanam would exclusively decide the members of the team to light the lamp on November 24.

It ordered that the composition and number of the team would be settled by the Madurai Collector in consultation with the temple’s Executive Officer, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the Commissioner of Police, Madurai.
The Collector would act as the nodal officer for the event.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu Government Moves Supreme Court Challenging Madras HC Order To Remove Periyar Statue From Temple Land
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Tamil Nadu Government has approached the Supreme Court challenging the Madras High Court's order directing the removal of a statue of Dravidian movement leader and reformer EV Ramasamy, popularly known as Periyar, installed near the Arulmigu Bramasirakandeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur district.

The Madras High Court, by its order dated October 30, 2026, had directed the Thanjavur District Collector to safely remove the statue from the temple land and relocate it to another suitable place within four weeks.
The Court had also directed the State authorities to file a compliance report and listed the matter after four weeks to verify compliance.

The Division Bench comprising Justices P Velmurugan and K Ramakrishnan passed the order while hearing a writ petition filed by Rama Ravikumar, a devotee, seeking the removal of the statue from the temple premises.

The petitioner had sought the removal of the statue in light of a recommendation made by the Joint Commissioner of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department, Thanjavur, in proceedings dated July 8, 2026.
The petitioner had alleged that the statue was installed by the Dravidar Kazhagam in 1990 without obtaining the necessary permission from the HR&CE Department.
He had also objected to the inscription beneath the statue, which carries Periyar's statement denying the existence of God.

During the proceedings, the High Court had directed the District Collector to conduct a physical inspection of the location and ascertain whether the statue stood on temple land or government poramboke land.
The authorities subsequently informed the Court that the statue was situated on land belonging to the temple and not on government poramboke land.

Taking note of the status report submitted by the District Collector, the Bench observed that the statue had been installed on temple land without obtaining permission from the temple authorities, the District Collector or any other competent authority.
Accordingly, the Court directed the District Collector to remove the statue safely and relocate it to another suitable place within four weeks.
The Court disposed of the writ petition with the above directions and ordered the matter to be listed after four weeks for reporting compliance.
